images.title: Bark plates, fissures and moss
images.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Project: Leafline. These are newly made concept/reference and store-page images, never in-game textures.
Shared art direction, reused from the initial set: grounded stylized realism with a painterly cinematic finish, attractive readable large shapes, credible macro-scale nature, warm brown bark and green leaves. Tree forms should feel feasible with procedural geometry and math/shader-driven surfaces: strong bark ridges and branching silhouettes, restrained microdetail.
Current design: summer canopy, warm plated bark with deep fissures and patches of moss, backlit green leaves. An ordinary full-sized tree is enormous beside a millimetre-long ant: broad bark plates and a trunk whose curvature disappears beyond the frame. Use the intimate close-to-bark perspective of a camera looking up a real trunk, with mild depth of field that preserves readable surfaces.
Leafcutter identity when present: dark reddish-brown Atta worker, large heart-shaped head, elbowed antennae, strong mandibles, small dorsal thorax spines, narrow TWO-SEGMENT waist, oval gaster, exactly six legs in three pairs from the thorax. Natural insect anatomy without human hands, faces or clothing.
Carrying rule when present: exactly one CUT leaf fragment gripped at its lower edge in the mandibles and held UPRIGHT ABOVE THE HEAD, a vertical sail catching light, never flat out in front, never a whole leaf on a stem, never in a backpack or on a pole.
Scent rule when present: a THIN restrained translucent cyan trace hugging the bark surface, subordinate to the environment, never a neon rope or raised rail.
Constraints: original art, no text at all, no lettering, logos, trademarks, watermarks or UI. No weapons, rockets, birds, injuries, animal harm, nest interior, villages or fantasy architecture. No collage or multi-panel board.
Asset type: close material study for a procedural math/shader bark material, reference only, not a usable game texture. Output: one landscape material illustration.
Primary request: a flat, evenly lit close study at ant scale of warm brown bark plates, deep fissures and sparse moss. NO CHARACTERS.
Composition: the entire image is a close section of one continuous trunk surface, viewed nearly straight on with only gentle curvature. Large irregular elongated bark plates fill the image, separated by branching dark fissures. Give the plates broad climbable tops and subtly layered angular edges; vary their width and length without obvious tiling. Include a few small olive-green moss patches concentrated in shaded fissures and plate junctions. Fine grain is subordinate to the larger forms and should suggest something achievable through analytic ridges and layered shader noise.
Lighting: neutral diffuse daylight spread evenly across the whole surface, soft local occlusion inside fissures, NO dramatic spotlights, dappled shadows, sun shafts or glossy wetness. Warm ochre-brown plate tops, deeper umber crevices, restrained muted green moss. Keep all the surface in clear focus.
Constraints: no ants or other animals, no scent trace, leaves, sky, ground, tools, labels, charts, swatches, grid, seams, text or frame. One cohesive continuous material study, not a board of several samples.

Composition: a single near-flat broad ovate leaf blade fills most of the image against a simple quiet desaturated green background. Show the complete blade silhouette and short petiole, a strong central midrib, paired branching secondary veins and finer hierarchical veins. The far edge has subtle natural serrations. Along the near edge are exactly three clear rounded cut-outs, one small, one medium and one larger circular bite, as if useful fragments have been removed; these are leafcutter cut shapes, smooth intentional arcs rather than rot, ragged tearing or holes scattered across the leaf interior. Keep sufficient intact leaf area to understand the original leaf shape.
Lighting: broad diffuse EVEN backlighting across the lamina, making thin regions luminous yellow-green and the vein hierarchy softly darker. No localized sun flare, harsh cast shadows, theatrical spotlight or deep atmospheric blur. A thin lighter fresh edge at each circular bite shows the cut thickness. Front fill keeps the whole leaf readable.
Materials: natural matte green lamina, subtle variation, restrained analytic-looking vein structure suitable to reproduce with UV mathematics, without photographic dirt or surface droplets.
Constraints: no ants, insects, hands, tools, scene vignette, scent line, detached fragments, labels, arrows, UI, swatches, grid, lettering or text. One cohesive leaf study, not a collage.
